name: accept-approved-by
description: A refund request under alice's root grant, with an approved_by claim her approval record proves; replay checked.

name: accept-tests-passed-t2
description: The accept message plus tests_passed proven by a result the tool executor wrote (T2).

name: accept-unproven-no-evidence
description: The accept message plus a tests_passed claim with no evidence.

name: accept-unproven-t1-result
description: tests_passed whose only result is the agent's own report (T1).

name: accept-unproven-unplaced-tool
description: tests_passed run by the executor through mcp:ci/run, a tool the placement table does not list as shell.

name: reject-strict-required-unproven
description: strict: the schema requires approved_by and the claim has no evidence.

name: reject-envelope-extra-field
description: A field the envelope does not have, added after signing.

name: reject-envelope-pcm-false
description: pcm set to false after signing: it must be the integer 0.

name: reject-forged-signature
description: amount changed after signing, signature kept.

name: reject-unpinned-key
description: A valid message; trust pins only another log's key.

name: reject-grant-signature-as-message
description: The message body signed for the grant purpose (pcm.grant.v0) with the test log key, offline.

name: reject-unknown-schema
description: A valid refund.quote; the receiver has only the refund.request schema.

name: reject-schema-extra-field
description: Args with an arg the schema does not list.

name: reject-schema-int-as-string
description: Args with order as the string "81".

name: reject-schema-bool-as-int
description: Args with order as true, a bool for an int field.

name: reject-schema-money-over-max
description: Args with amount 1000001, over the max 1000000.

name: reject-replay-duplicate-nonce
description: The receiver already took this message: its nonce was seen.

name: reject-replay-outside-window
description: Checked 600 s after it was signed, with a 300 s window.

name: reject-replay-before-started
description: Signed 1 s before the receiver started.

name: reject-wrong-recipient
description: Addressed to uid:990102, checked by uid:990103.

name: reject-replay-no-real-time
description: ts set to month 13 and re-signed with the test log key (the signer takes ts from its clock): the TS pattern lets it through, the replay check refuses it.

name: reject-grant-amount-over-caveat
description: amount 50000 under a grant of amount <= 20000.

name: reject-grant-expired
description: Signed after its root grant expired (a grant made to expire in 3 s).

name: reject-grant-cross-tenant
description: A root grant carol approved in a run of tenant acme, used by a sender in tenant default.

name: reject-grant-root-by-agent
description: The root grant's issuer kind edited to agent and re-signed with the test log key (the signer issues root grants only from a person's approval).

name: reject-grant-subject-not-sender
description: A root grant for uid:990102, sent by uid:990101.

name: accept-delegation-narrowing
description: Two steps: alice's delegable grant to A (amount <= 20000), A's child to B (amount <= 15000); B asks for 12000.

name: reject-delegation-over-child-cap
description: The same chain; B asks for 18000, within the root's cap but over the child's.

name: reject-grant-widening-child
description: A's child to B raises the cap to 30000; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-widen-and-tighten-child
description: A's child to B raises the cap to 30000 and adds amount >= 100; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-missing-caveat-child
description: A's child to B drops order == 81; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-below-non-delegable
description: A child below alice's grant that can't be passed on; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key under the non-delegable root.

name: reject-grant-broken-parent
description: A real child placed under another real root, so its parent hash names another grant.

name: reject-claim-changed-record-hash
description: approved_by whose record hash has one hex digit changed.

name: reject-claim-cut-proof
description: approved_by whose inclusion proof lost its last hash.

name: reject-claim-unpinned-log-note
description: approved_by under a checkpoint note of a log trust does not pin.

name: reject-claim-evidence-from-another-log
description: The same claim, with trust pinning both logs: the note is not of the log that signed the message.

name: reject-grant-from-another-log
description: A root grant alice approved on the other log, for uid:990101 there, sent by uid:990101 of the test log; trust pins both logs. Identities are names inside one log: the grant is not this sender's.

name: accept-replay-same-agent-other-log
description: The receiver first took a message from uid:990101 of the other log with the nonce of this one (re-signed with the other log's test key); trust pins both logs. A sender is the pair (log key, agent), so uid:990101 of the test log is another sender and its nonce is new.

name: reject-claim-proof-non-canonical-base64
description: approved_by whose first proof entry has an unused bit of its last base64 character set: the same 32 bytes, but only canonical base64 is taken.

name: reject-claim-witnesses-required-unmet
description: approved_by under a note with no cosignature; trust requires one witness.

name: reject-claim-wrong-person
description: approved_by naming bob; the approval record is alice's.

name: reject-claim-approval-of-another-call
description: approved_by of call grant-2, with alice's approval of grant-1 as evidence.

name: reject-claim-pytest-or-true
description: tests_passed of `pytest ... || true`, run by the executor (T2): its status is not the tests'.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-unmapped-identity
description: approved_by naming uid:990009, an approver no person in the signer's approvals configuration maps to, with its approval record as evidence: only a person's name proves it.

name: accept-witnessed
description: approved_by under a note cosigned by the pinned witness; trust requires one witness.

name: reject-claim-malformed-unpinned-note-line
description: approved_by under a note with an extra signature line of a key trust does not pin, whose signature is 3 bytes: a malformed line fails the note even when its key is not pinned.

name: reject-claim-record-not-an-event
description: approved_by whose approval record has the number 5 as its prev_hash, which no claim checker reads, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited record: a record that is no valid tracekit.event.v2 event fails.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-malformed-no-evidence
description: tests_passed of `pytest ... || true` with no evidence: a suite that is no test command is malformed, so the claim fails without evidence too.

name: reject-claim-file-written-relative-no-evidence
description: file_written of the relative path work/report.txt with no evidence: the claim is malformed, so it fails without evidence too.

name: reject-claim-bash-c
description: tests_passed of `bash -c 'pytest || true'`, run by the executor (T2): bash is not a test runner.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-comment
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py # || true`, run by the executor (T2): a suite may hold no `#`, even where the shell reads a comment, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-hash-inside-word
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py#|| true`, run by the executor (T2): a `#` inside a word starts no comment, so the shell runs `|| true`, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-background
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py &`, run by the executor (T2): the shell runs the tests in the background and exits 0 whatever they do, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-ansi-c-quote
description: tests_passed of `pytest $'\'';true #'`, run by the executor (T2): sh reads `$'\''` as one quote and runs `true`, where Python's shlex reads one word, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-unbalanced-quote
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q 'tests/test_refund.py`, run by the executor (T2): its quotes don't balance, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-dot-slash
description: tests_passed of `./pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): the program must be the runner's bare name, not a file of that name, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-runner-path
description: tests_passed of `.venv/bin/pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): the program must be the runner's bare name, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-co
description: tests_passed of `pytest --co -q`, run by the executor (T2): --co is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-collect-only
description: tests_passed of `pytest --collect-only -q`, run by the executor (T2): --collect-only is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-help
description: tests_passed of `pytest --help -q`, run by the executor (T2): --help is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-h
description: tests_passed of `pytest -h -q`, run by the executor (T2): -h is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-version
description: tests_passed of `pytest --version -q`, run by the executor (T2): --version is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-V
description: tests_passed of `pytest -V -q`, run by the executor (T2): -V is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-he
description: tests_passed of `pytest --he -q`, run by the executor (T2): --he is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-wrapper
description: tests_passed of `uv run pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): a wrapper in front is not in the list of test commands.

name: accept-tests-passed-npm-test
description: tests_passed of `npm test`, run by the executor (T2).

name: accept-tests-passed-python-m-pytest
description: tests_passed of `python3 -m pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2).

name: reject-claim-tests-failed
description: tests_passed whose T2 result is an error.

name: reject-claim-salt-without-args
description: tests_passed whose decision record carries its salt but not its args.

name: reject-claim-opening-wrong-args
description: tests_passed whose opening carries other args than the decision committed to.

name: reject-claim-decision-without-id
description: tests_passed whose policy.decision and tool.result records both lost data.decision_id, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records: a decision without its id matches no call, though the two still pair by their missing ids.

name: accept-file-written
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), with the SHA-256 of the content written.

name: reject-claim-file-written-wrong-digest
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), with another digest than the content's.

name: reject-claim-file-written-dotdot
description: file_written of /work/../work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), naming the path with `..`, which fails.

name: reject-claim-file-written-relative
description: file_written of work/report.txt by a Write of work/report.txt the executor ran (T2): the paths are equal, but a relative claim is malformed, so it fails.

name: accept-unproven-file-written-relative-call
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of report.txt the executor ran (T2): the record doesn't hold the working directory, so the relative path may name this file or another.

name: accept-reached-host-observed
description: reached_host proven by the effect.observed record an egress observer reported to the signer.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-unreadable-claim
description: reached_host of a..example with the observed evidence: a host with an empty label won't parse, so the claim is unproven.

name: accept-reached-host-http
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of https://API.Example.COM:8443/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): the host is read lower case, without the port.

name: accept-reached-host-claim-port
description: reached_host api.example.com:443 by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): a port in the claim is ignored too.

name: accept-reached-host-trailing-dot
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com./v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): the host loses its one trailing dot.

name: accept-reached-host-short-ipv4
description: reached_host 127.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://127.1/health the executor ran (T2): 127.1 is the IPv4 address 127.0.0.1.

name: accept-reached-host-idn
description: reached_host xn--bcher-kva.example by a WebFetch of http://bücher.example/ the executor ran (T2): the host goes to ASCII by IDNA, so it is the punycode name the claim carries.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-other-host
description: reached_host api.example.org by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): another host.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket
description: reached_host good.com by a WebFetch of http://[x]@good.com/ the executor ran (T2): a `[` in the userinfo: Python's urlsplit refuses the URL, so its host won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ambiguous
description: reached_host b.example by a WebFetch of http://a.example\@b.example/ the executor ran (T2): a browser reads the host a.example and Python's urllib b.example, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-deviation
description: reached_host fass.example by a WebFetch of http://faß.example/ the executor ran (T2): IDNA 2003 maps the sharp s to ss and a browser keeps it (xn--fa-hia.example), so a host with one of the four deviation characters won't parse.

name: accept-reached-host-unassigned
description: reached_host xn--x-qib.example by a WebFetch of http://x͸.example/ the executor ran (T2): U+0378 is unassigned in Unicode 3.2, and the stdlib codec takes it (AllowUnassigned on).

name: reject-claim-reached-host-file-url
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of file://api.example.com/x the executor ran (T2): a file: URL has no host a browser reads.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-no-ipv6
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://%5b::1%5d/ the executor ran (T2): percent-decoded, the host is `[`, which is no IPv6 address, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-nul
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://api.example.com%00.evil/ the executor ran (T2): percent-decoded, the host holds a NUL, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-claim-bad-port
description: reached_host of api.example.com:abc with the observed evidence: a port must be 1 to 5 digits, so the claim won't parse.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-too-long
description: reached_host of a 200-character host: a claim's host is an id, at most 128 characters.

name: reject-sig-non-canonical-base64
description: sig.sig with an unused bit of its last base64 character set: the same 64 bytes, but only canonical base64 is taken, so a signature has one text form.

name: reject-small-order-key
description: trust pins a key that is the identity point (small order). The signature R = identity, S = 0 holds for any message under the plain equation; a verifier must refuse the key.

name: accept-identity-line-break-chars
description: to.agent holds a carriage return and U+2028: an identity's subject is any character but a line feed.

name: accept-jcs-payload
description: A data payload with floats, a non-ASCII key, a key outside the BMP that sorts before U+E000 by UTF-16 code units, controls and U+2028: the signature verifies only with exact RFC 8785.

name: reject-replay-floor-arrival-order
description: per_sender 1, no window: the receiver took the 3rd, then the 1st message, so the 3rd left first and raised the floor to its time; the 2nd is older than the floor.

name: accept-schema-field-types
description: A string, id, enum, bool and time field, and an optional field left out.

name: reject-schema-field-types
description: Each field of the same schema broken: a title of 81 characters, a code the pattern refuses, a level not in the enum, 0 for a bool, a time without microseconds, an optional field too long.

name: reject-grant-needed
description: refund.request needs a grant (grant: true); the message has none.

name: reject-grant-tampered
description: alice's root grant, with delegable set to true after signing.

name: reject-grant-unpinned-key
description: alice's root grant, signed by the other log, which trust does not pin.

name: reject-grant-issuer-is-subject
description: alice's root grant, with its issuer id edited to its subject, re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-bad-caveat
description: alice's root grant, with an `in` caveat on a money field, re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-other-intent
description: A root grant for refund.quote, sent with a refund.request.

name: accept-delegation-less-than
description: A's child to B has amount < 20001, which narrows amount <= 20000.

name: reject-grant-child-outlives-parent
description: A's child to B expires 60 s after its parent; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-child-wrong-issuer
description: A's child to B names uid:990107, not the parent's subject, as its issuer; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.
